reading.body:
Flexential's Hillsboro 4 expansion in Portland publishes 36 MW of IT capacity today with 54 MW of additional critical capacity planned, positioning it as the fourth-largest published data center campus in Oregon by capacity. The facility sits in a 138,000 square foot footprint with a larger 358,000 square foot technical footprint, suggesting significant room for further buildout. At 40 kW per rack as a common density for mixed workloads, the 36 MW current capacity represents roughly 900 racks, with the planned 54 MW expansion potentially adding 1,350 racks; together these would make roughly 2,250 racks or equivalently 18,000 H100-equivalent accelerators at four accelerators per kilowatt.

The campus holds certifications for security compliance including HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, NIST 800-53, and ITAR, as well as attestations for audit readiness including SOC 1 Type II, SOC 3, and SSAE 18. These certifications qualify the facility to host regulated workloads including government-classified work and financial services, but do not indicate which tenants are present. Oregon publishes only eight data center campuses with disclosed capacity across 133 mapped facilities statewide, for a total of 156.6 MW of published capacity; Hillsboro 4 represents 23 percent of the state's disclosed supply in existing capacity alone.

The campus is not published as grid-connected to a specific utility or power source, and planned expansion timing is not specified. Whether the planned 54 MW expansion depends on new power infrastructure or draws from existing supply in the Portland area is not disclosed by the operator.
